claims.claim: Beam is a sparse mixture-of-experts model with 501B total and 23B active parameters across 52 layers, text-only.
Beam was pretrained on 23.8 trillion tokens.
Beam was pretrained end-to-end in under four weeks on a cluster of 6,144 NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 GPUs, with goodput reaching 92.3% towards the end.
Beam's high-compute RL run generated over 100 million rollouts on 10.5K NVIDIA GB300 GPUs over 4 weeks.
Reflection claims Beam achieves scores comparable to GLM-5.2 on advanced reasoning benchmarks while using 3-4x less inference compute.

Reflection estimates inference FLOPs as 2 x active parameter count x mean generated tokens per attempt over DeepSWE, HLE and Terminal Bench 2.1, excluding prefill, context-dependent attention and serving overhead.
GLM-5.2 has 744B total and 40B active parameters.
GLM-5.2 uses 43k output tokens per Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index task, of which 37k is reasoning, up from 26k for GLM-5.1.
A GB300 NVL72 rack of 72 GPUs is rated 360 PFLOPS FP16/BF16 with sparsity, implying 2.5 PFLOPS dense BF16 per GPU.
DeepSeek-V3 (37B active) was pretrained on 14.8T tokens using 2,664K H800 GPU-hours.
NVIDIA reported Megatron Core reaching 1,648 TFLOPS per GPU pretraining DeepSeek-V3 671B on GB300 NVL72.
Llama 3 405B training achieved 38-43% BF16 model FLOPs utilization and used 3.8e25 FLOPs.
The EU AI Act presumes systemic risk for general-purpose AI models whose cumulative training compute exceeds 10^25 FLOPs.
In Reflection's table Beam scores 36.2 on HLE (no tools) versus 40.5 for GLM-5.2, and trails GLM-5.2 on AIME 2026, GPQA Diamond and CritPt.
Z.ai's GLM-5.2 card reports Terminal Bench 2.1 (Terminus-2) at 81.0 and DeepSWE at 46.2, while Artificial Analysis measured Terminal Bench 2.1 at 78%.
Qwen 3.8-Max is a 2.4T-total, 95B-active mixture-of-experts model.
Kimi K3 has 2.8T total and 104B activated parameters.
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash activates 8B parameters per token during prefill and 16B during decode.
In Reflection's own table DeepSeek V4.1 Flash beats Beam on HLE (39.1 vs 36.2), Terminal Bench 2.1 (90.6 vs 80.1) and DeepSWE (74.2 vs 44.4).

Reflection's SpaceX compute deal pays $150M per month from July 2026 through 2029 for up to $6.3B of GB300 capacity at Colossus 2, and either side can exit with 90 days' notice after the first three months.
Nebius agreed to sell Reflection more than $1B of GB300 capacity through 2029.
Reflection raised $2B at an $8B valuation in October 2025; Reuters corrected its story to remove Nvidia as a lead investor.
In October 2025 Reflection said it was aiming to release its first frontier model early the next year.
Reflection has raised roughly $4.7B per PitchBook and its last round valued it at $25B pre-money; its performance claims have not been independently verified.
Reflection will release Beam's weights under Apache 2.0, with technical report and model card, later in October 2026; the model is in final red-teaming with waitlisted early access.
OpenAI stopped reporting SWE-bench Verified in February 2026, citing flawed tests and contamination, and recommended SWE-bench Pro.
Chinese open models reached 1.15B cumulative Hugging Face downloads versus 723M for US models by March 2026.
Z.ai lists GLM-5.2 at $1.40 per 1M input tokens and $4.40 per 1M output tokens.
GLM-5.2's IndexShare reuses one sparse-attention indexer across every four layers, which Z.ai says cuts per-token FLOPs 2.9x at 1M context.
Kaplan et al. give per-token forward compute as 2N plus a context-dependent attention term 2 n_layer n_ctx d_attn.
Artificial Analysis said early indicators suggest Beam will be one of the most token-efficient open models it has seen for its level of intelligence, without publishing scores.
Aleph Alpha's Kolibri-1 was pretrained on 768 B200 GPUs for 21 days (392k GPU-hours) with 6.4e23 total FLOPs.
Artificial Analysis called GLM-5.2 the most verbose of the leading models, using about 141M output tokens to run its Intelligence Index, about 1.8x the average.
Beam's pretraining compute under the 6ND approximation is about 3.28e24 FLOPs.
assumptions: Standard 6 x active parameters x tokens training approximation; excludes attention FLOPs, ablations and midtraining

claims.claim: 6,144 GPUs for 28 days is at most 4,128,768 GPU-hours of pretraining.
assumptions: 'Under four weeks' taken as an upper bound of 28 days of full-cluster use

claims.claim: If the full cluster ran 28 days, Beam's pretraining delivered about 221 TFLOPS per GPU.
assumptions: Full cluster busy for 28 days; 6ND FLOPs

claims.claim: That throughput is about 8.8% of a GB300's dense BF16 peak.
assumptions: Dense BF16 peak = rack sparse BF16 / 72 / 2

claims.claim: DeepSeek-V3's pretraining delivered about 343 TFLOPS per H800 under the same 6ND convention.
At NVIDIA's 1,648 TFLOPS-per-GPU GB300 record, 6,144 GPUs would complete Beam's 6ND pretraining compute in about 3.75 days.
assumptions: Benchmark throughput sustained over a production run; record precision unstated

claims.claim: Beam's RL run used about 7.06M GPU-hours, 1.71x the pretraining GPU budget.
assumptions: Both phases ran for the same ~4 weeks; 10.5K taken as 10,500

claims.claim: GLM-5.2's active parameters are 1.74x Beam's.
For a 3x compute advantage under Reflection's formula, GLM-5.2 must generate 1.725x Beam's tokens per attempt.
assumptions: FLOPs = 2 x active params x generated tokens

claims.claim: For a 4x compute advantage, GLM-5.2 must generate 2.3x Beam's tokens per attempt.
assumptions: FLOPs = 2 x active params x generated tokens

claims.claim: 6,144 GPUs is 85.33 NVL72 racks, not a whole number of racks.
Beam's 6ND pretraining compute is about 0.33x the EU AI Act 1e25 systemic-risk threshold.
assumptions: Pretraining only; RL and other cumulative compute not counted

claims.claim: Per token, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash's decode-active compute is 0.70x Beam's.
Qwen 3.8-Max's active parameters are 4.13x Beam's.
